_note: Narration script for the paramedic TBI module (CPG-144-P v1.0). Lee voice on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences, pitched at paramedic level. The prompt sent to ElevenLabs starts with the [calmly] tag and spells GCS, ECG, BGL, SpO2, EtCO2, RDR, ICP, CVA, MTT, DTT, EOC and SAAS as letters, and mL/kg as "mils per kilo"; captions use the text here.

lines.head: Secondary insults
sentences: The primary injury happened before you arrived.
What you can change is what happens next.
Hypoglycaemia, bleeding, cerebral oedema and seizures.
Hypoxia or hypercarbia, and hypotension, predict a poor outcome.

lines.head: Cerebral perfusion
sentences: So it's all about cerebral perfusion.
An adequate blood pressure, with no hypotension.
And no rises in intracranial pressure.
The injured brain may have lost its autoregulation.
So the blood pressure you maintain really matters.

lines.head: Monitoring
sentences: Monitor the GCS, ECG and BGL.
In a spontaneously breathing patient, the numbers may be unreliable.

lines.head: Fluids
sentences: Saline in 250 mL aliquots, up to 20 mL/kg.
Aim for a MAP of 90 or more, or a systolic of 110 or more.
10 mL/kg aliquots, to a max of 250 mL.
Aim for a normal systolic for age, using the RDR.

lines.head: Venous return
sentences: Straining and gagging raise intracranial pressure.
So does anything that slows drainage from the head.
Sit them 30 degrees head up, if their condition permits.

lines.head: The agitated patient
sentences: It can stop you assessing and treating in time.
Then get clinical support early, for potential sedation.
It picks up hypoventilation before hypoxia shows.
And remember, sedatives and opiates are synergistic.

lines.head: Hypoxic brain injury
sentences: This guideline also covers sudden hypoxic brain injury.
Think CVA, intracerebral bleed, drowning or hanging.
Strongly consider consulting the SAAS Medical Practitioner.

lines.head: Support and transport
sentences: Consult the EOC Clinician for a treatment plan.
Notify as per the MTT or DTT.
Out here, that's the local hospital, or trauma bypass.
And MedSTAR is notified through the EOC.
